targetAudience.primary: Engineers and governance leads responsible for long-running digital employees
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands checkpoints, agent context, workspaces and external tool effects.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A technically restorable snapshot can be mistaken for proof that resumption is authorized, causally consistent and safe.

whyNow: AgentRewind reports gains from restoring aligned agent context and controlled workspace state on 82 long-horizon engineering tasks, while explicitly leaving network and external-service effects outside the rollback boundary.

externalHook.description: A rewind may restore files and context while leaving already-committed external effects untouched.

coreProposition: Causally aligned context and workspace checkpoints are necessary for evaluated long-horizon recovery, but accountable resumption also requires occurrence-bound authority and reconciliation of effects outside the snapshot boundary.

originalValue.description: Extends checkpoint alignment into a recovery contract binding occurrence identity, current authority, execution evidence and external-effect reconciliation.

readerTakeaway: Treat restoration as one mechanism, not the whole authorization; bind snapshot, epoch, policy, principal and effect ledger before resuming.

supported: Aligned context/workspace rewind is reported and evaluated on 82 tasks.
The rollback boundary covers the workspace, not network or external-service state.
Ablations report complementary value from environment rewind, context rewind and rewind memory.
unsupported: A complete recovery protocol evaluated in production
uncertain: When recovery becomes a new work occurrence

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument concerns general recovery governance.

decisionReason: The research supplies a concrete mechanism, measured results and an explicit boundary from which a bounded governance design follows.
